description: Validates that the mts-reference skill improves Claude's ability to answer MTS documentation and migration questions over a broad set of realistic scenarios.

evals.name: doservice-transport-classification
evals.prompt: I'm looking at a BUK Spring Boot service called scp-eps-fullserve-buk. I found this call: serviceManager.doService("RETRIEVECUSTOMER", "GET_CUSTOMER_FULL", requestEdo). The dependency tree includes egs-ods-customer-mf.jar in the Gradle cache. What transport pattern is this and how should I document the TDL tables and WMID parameters?
evals.expected_output: Should identify transport as mainframe-mq, explain the WMID-CUST-PRM → TDLCUST mapping, describe the 3-tier confidence approach for compiled JAR extraction, and reference the doService pattern structure (serviceManager.doService(SERVICE_NAME, methodName, requestEdo)).

assertions.description: Response identifies transport pattern as mainframe-mq (or equivalent mainframe MQ description)
assertions.check: contains any of: mainframe-mq, mainframe MQ, IBM MQ, CICS mainframe

assertions.description: Response references WMID parameters or WMID-CUST-PRM specifically
assertions.check: contains any of: WMID, WMID-CUST-PRM

assertions.description: Response mentions TDL tables or TDLCUST
assertions.check: contains any of: TDL, TDLCUST, TDL table

assertions.description: Response demonstrates understanding of EBS/EGS framework
assertions.check: contains any of: EBS, EGS, Enterprise Business Service, Enterprise Gateway Service

evals.name: compiled-jar-extraction-approach
evals.prompt: I'm trying to document a BUK Spring Boot application's EGS service. The Gradle cache only has the compiled egs-ods-accounts-mf.jar (no -sources.jar). I need to find out which WMID parameters the AccountsTransaction class uses and what the program code and version code are. How should I approach this without source code?
evals.expected_output: Should describe the 3-tier compiled JAR extraction approach: Tier 1 (constant pool parser for WMID strings), Tier 2 (ROP/RIP files for authoritative lists with types), Tier 3 (javap for exact program/version codes). Should mention confidence levels and that Tier 3 requires javap on the system.

assertions.description: Response mentions constant pool parsing or Tier 1 approach
assertions.check: contains any of: constant pool, Tier 1, .class bytes, zipfile

assertions.description: Response mentions ROP/RIP files (Tier 2)
assertions.check: contains any of: ROP, RIP, riprop, Tier 2

assertions.description: Response mentions javap for exact values (Tier 3)
assertions.check: contains any of: javap, Tier 3, getProgramCode, getVersionCode

assertions.description: Response mentions confidence levels/tags for extracted data
assertions.check: contains any of: confidence, verified-from-bytecode, partial-from-bytecode, verified-from-rop-rip

evals.name: api-replacement-search-strategy
evals.prompt: I need to find an ODS API replacement for an MTS service that reads from TDLCUST and TDLCORD tables. The service is called CustomerAddressRetrieveGateway and it returns customer name, address lines, and correspondence address. What's the best way to search for candidate replacement APIs in the Backstage catalogue?

evals.name: variable-method-tracing-pattern3
evals.prompt: In scp-eps-idv, I see a doService call where the method name is a variable: serviceDelegate.doService(SERVICE_NAME, callingMethod, params). The variable callingMethod comes from a method parameter. How do I find all the concrete method names that get passed to this doService call?
evals.expected_output: Should describe Pattern 3 (variable method name), explain that the discovery agent must trace back through callers to find all concrete values passed as callingMethod, mention that each unique (service, method) pair becomes a separate entry in the discovery output, and note the multiplexer pattern where one doService call site maps to multiple services.

evals.name: gateway-equivalence-scoring
evals.prompt: I'm running api-replacement-match for CustomerGateway.findByPrimaryKey. The top candidate from Backstage is sodscustenq. When I search sodscustenq's GitLab repo, I find that its source code contains references to CustomerGateway and the transaction name CUS_ALL_RETRIEVE. How should this affect the match scoring?
evals.expected_output: Should describe the gateway-equivalence boost: finding the same gateway class name gives +10% and finding the same transaction name gives +5%. Should explain that this proves the ODS API wraps the same EGS gateway, making it the architecturally correct replacement. Should note that gateway_equivalent=true is set on the candidate.

assertions.check: contains any of: CUS_ALL_RETRIEVE, transaction name, CICS code

assertions.description: Response references searching GitLab source code for evidence
assertions.check: contains any of: GitLab, source code, blob search, Step A2

evals.name: soap-webservice-transport-classification
evals.prompt: I found a doService call in a BUK Spring Boot app that routes through MortgagesGateway.retrieveAccountDetails(). The EGS source JAR (egs_mortgages) contains a ServiceAssembler class and an X61563ProxyServiceWrapper class. There's no getProgramCode() or getVersionCode() method — no CICS transaction pattern at all. The gateway doesn't use WMID parameters or TDL tables. What transport pattern is this and how should I document it?
evals.expected_output: Should identify transport as soap-webservice (not mainframe-mq), explain that the ProxyServiceWrapper/ServiceAssembler pattern indicates a SOAP call to a non-CICS backend (ILP/Hogan), note there are no TDL tables or DataGroups, and describe the Section 6 variant as Backend Mappings (SOAP Web Service Mappings).

assertions.check: contains any of: soap-webservice, SOAP web service, SOAP Web Service

assertions.description: Response distinguishes from mainframe-mq
assertions.check: contains any of: not mainframe, non-CICS, no CICS, not MQ

assertions.description: Response identifies backend system type
assertions.check: contains any of: ILP, Hogan, non-CICS backend, external SOAP

assertions.description: Response notes no TDL tables for this transport
assertions.check: contains any of: no TDL, N/A, no DataGroup, no WMID

evals.name: spec-repo-discovery-from-backstage-slug

When I search for openapi or swagger blobs in that repo, I find nothing — it's just a thin Spring Boot app. But the service doc says this is the correct replacement. How do I find the API specification?
evals.expected_output: Should describe the spec repo discovery pattern (Step A0): derive spec repo path by replacing apps/ with spec/ and appending -spec suffix (barclays/cct-collg-servicing-apis/spec/rc-colleague-eligibility-api-spec), check if the repo exists via get_repository_tree, look for openapi.yaml under oas/ directory, then resolve $ref components (parameters.yaml, response model YAML, example JSON). Should mention Pattern 1 (name-spec) is most common, Pattern 2 (no suffix) as fallback, and Pattern 3 (search_repositories) as last resort.

evals.name: ods-graphql-schema-field-verification
evals.prompt: I'm running api-replacement-match for LoansEnquiryService.retrieveBalanceDetails. The service reads the outstanding principal balance from the ALS backend using DAG field AMWKWI00-WI-TOT-PRIN. The Backstage search returned no strong REST API candidates for ALS loan balance data. Is there any ODS API that exposes ALS loan data I could use for field-level verification?
evals.expected_output: Should mention the ODS GraphQL API (sodsgraphql) as a reference source for ALS loan data. Should describe that the GraphQL schema at barclays/ods-apis/app/sodsgraphql contains an AlsAccountHolding type with fields like outstandingPrincipal that have lineage annotations back to ALS source tables (TEJVRT02.RT_TOT_PRIN). Should mention the schema files are at src/main/resources/schema/retail-account-detail.graphql and that the query path is retailCustomer.productHolding.alsAccountHoldings.
